title: God's workmanship (Ephesians 2:1–10)
hookLine: saved by grace through faith; we are his poem, made for good works
tomorrow: Paul says a wall came down. but which wall?

lines: A BOWL RISES FROM THE CLAY.
cards: A pottery wheel, spinning. The teacher's wet hands close around a lump of clay, and a bowl rises out of it that wasn't there a minute ago. Nobody asks the bowl to earn its shape.

It was made that way, on purpose, for holding things. Paul has a word for that. But he starts chapter two of Ephesians somewhere much darker: "And you hath he quickened, who were dead in trespasses and sins."
And then two small words, right where the story turns.

teach.b: "But God, who is rich in mercy, for his great love wherewith he loved us." But God. The dead don't raise themselves; somebody else has to act.

teach.h: BY GRACE, THE GIFT OF GOD.
teach.b: Then the sentence at the center: "For by grace are ye saved through faith; and that not of yourselves: it is the gift of God: Not of works, lest any man should boast." A gift, with nothing to brag about.
So why bother doing good at all?
The very next line: "For we are his workmanship, created in Christ Jesus unto good works, which God hath before ordained that we should walk in them." Not saved by good works. Saved for them.
And the works aren't invented on the spot; Paul pictures them prepared ahead, like a path laid down before anyone walks it.
Here's one to tell a friend: Paul's Greek word for workmanship is poiema, a thing made. Some readers hear the English word poem in it and like the picture, a person as something God is writing.
Whatever the word history, the idea is right there in the verse. Churches put grace and works together in different words.

Catholic and Orthodox Christians speak of grace at work through a life of good works; some Protestant traditions stress that good works grow from grace as its fruit. This passage gives them all an order: a gift first.

how: Ephesians 2:8–10 is a passage some Christians learn by heart, and churches teach it when they explain how grace and good works fit together.

s: in Ephesians 2, good deeds are how you earn God's gift
the popular version. Paul says by grace, not of works; then, unto good works.

games.q: your little sister asks: 'if God's love is a free gift, why does mom make us volunteer at the shelter?' what fits Ephesians 2?
o: not to earn the gift: Paul says we're made for good works.
because volunteering is how we pay God back for the gift.
there's no reason; if it's free, good works don't matter.
games.why: by grace… not of works, then: we are his workmanship, created… unto good works. the gift comes first, and the good works are what the gift is for.

practice: Pick up one thing someone made by hand, or that you made: a mug, a drawing, a stitched hem. Look at it for the sit, at the marks of the maker and what it was made for.
Then let one good work already waiting in front of you this week come to mind.

wordCard.voice: God's workmanship. Paul's word for a person as something God made on purpose, for good works prepared ahead.

orig.note: Greek: a thing made, a work. Paul's word for his workmanship in Ephesians 2:10.

carryVoice: Carry this: his workmanship, made on purpose, for a purpose, with the good already waiting. See you soon.
